prerequisites: General knowledge about computer network operation
Knowledge about the transport layer of the TCP/IP protocol stack

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to write, develop and sign projects in the field of telecommunications engineering aimed at the conception and development or exploitation of telecommunication and electronics networks, services and applications.

Ability to work in a multidisciplinary group and in a multilingual environment and to communicate, both in writing and orally, knowledge, procedures, results and ideas related to telecommunications and electronics.

Ability to use communication and computer applications (office automation, databases, advanced calculation, project management, visualization, etc.) to support the development and exploitation of telecommunication and electronics networks, services and applications.
Ability to use computer tools for searching bibliographic resources or information related to telecommunications and electronics.

Ability to conceive, deploy, organize and manage telecommunication networks, systems, services and infrastructures in residential (home, city and digital communities), business or institutional contexts, taking responsibility for their implementation and continuous improvement, as well as knowing their economic and social impact.
Knowledge and use of the fundamentals of programming in telecommunication networks, systems and services.
Knowledge and use of the concepts of network architecture, communication protocols and interfaces.

Ability to differentiate the concepts of access and transport networks, circuit and packet switching networks, fixed and mobile networks, as well as distributed network systems and applications, voice, data, audio, video services and interactive and multimedia services.
Knowledge of telecommunications regulations and legislation at national, European and international levels.
Know and use the fundamentals of programming in telecommunication networks and services.
Establish appropriate network architecture for the correct functioning of communication services.
Select the most suitable transport layer protocol for a given application.
Identify application-level communication problems, as well as propose appropriate solutions to the problems encountered.
Interpret, analyze and relate the characteristics of web services, email services, naming services and other application-level services.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and refresh of the transport layer
The application layer in the TCP/IP protocol stack
Fundamentals of programming in networks and telecommunication services.
Design and programming of communication protocol prototypes.
Development of connection-oriented and datagram-based communication services programs.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary and extraordinary calls, the final grade is calculated as: Final Grade = 0.2 x TG + 0.4 x PL + 0.4 x TE, provided all minimums are met. All evaluated components (Theory exam, Laboratory practices, Group work) must be passed with a minimum of 5 out of 10. If any part is not passed, the final grade will be the highest score among the non-passed parts. Grades for passed blocks are saved between calls of the same academic year.
